expected.body: A 5-month-old infant with cystic fibrosis has frequent bulky stools and is brought in for failure to thrive. The mother notes easy bruising. Labs show ↑ PT/INR. Diagnosis: vitamin K deficiency from fat malabsorption. Key teaching: fat malabsorption leads to vitamin K deficiency, which reduces γ-carboxylation of clotting factors II, VII, IX, X, producing a bleeding diathesis.
